error.signature: AI tells an English-speaking foreigner in Finland to call the national Kriisipuhelin crisis line (09 2525 0111) expecting English-language support around the clock

verdict.summary: MIELI Mental Health Finland's national Kriisipuhelin (Crisis Helpline) operates a 24-hour phone number in Finnish (09 2525 0111) and a separate number in Swedish (09 2525 0112); MIELI's own contact page does not list English as available on either number. English-language crisis counselling is instead offered through MIELI Crisis Centre Helsinki, which only operates limited weekday hours (Mon-Thu 9am-12pm and 1-3pm, Fri 9am-12pm) - not 24/7. For an active life-threatening emergency, 112 (which does offer English-speaking operators) is the correct number, not the crisis line.

dead_ends.action: Give someone the number 09 2525 0111 as a 24/7 English-language mental health crisis line, the way a US 988 or UK Samaritans number might be assumed to work in English by default
dead_ends.why_fails: MIELI's own contact page lists 09 2525 0111 explicitly as the Finnish-language Kriisipuhelin number (24hrs) and 09 2525 0112 as the separate Swedish-language number; it does not list English on either number. A caller who does not speak Finnish or Swedish reaching this line may not get English-language support.
dead_ends.common_misconception: People assume any national crisis hotline defaults to English support for foreigners, or works the same 24/7 in every language the way it does in the local language.

dead_ends.action: Assume English-language crisis counselling in Finland is available at any hour, the same as the Finnish-language Kriisipuhelin
dead_ends.why_fails: MIELI's own crisis-helpline page states crisis counselling is offered 'in Finnish, Swedish, English and, if necessary, through an interpreter' via MIELI Crisis Centre Helsinki - but that service's booking line (09 4135 0510) only operates Mon-Thu 9am-12pm and 1pm-3pm, and Fri 9am-12pm. It is not a round-the-clock service like the Finnish Kriisipuhelin number.
dead_ends.condition: Contacting MIELI outside Mon-Fri daytime hours for English-language support

workarounds.action: For an active, life-threatening emergency (imminent risk of suicide, overdose in progress, someone unable to keep themselves safe right now), call 112 rather than the crisis line - 112 dispatches police/ambulance and has multilingual, often English-speaking, operators.
workarounds.how: State your location first, then describe the emergency, as with any 112 call.

workarounds.action: For non-emergency crisis support in English during the day, contact MIELI Crisis Centre Helsinki directly on 09 4135 0510 within its published hours (Mon-Thu 9am-12pm & 1pm-3pm, Fri 9am-12pm) to book English-language crisis counselling, rather than calling the 24/7 number and expecting English.
workarounds.tradeoff: Limited weekday hours mean no immediate English-language phone support outside that window; outside it, only the Finnish (and Swedish) 24/7 line or 112 for emergencies is available.

workarounds.action: If you speak Finnish or Swedish, or can access interpretation, the Kriisipuhelin numbers (09 2525 0111 Finnish, 09 2525 0112 Swedish) remain the correct round-the-clock, free, confidential option for non-emergency crisis support.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers the general EU-wide 112 emergency number replacing 911; this one covers the separate, non-emergency Kriisipuhelin mental-health crisis line and its limited English-language hours.
